dcat.description: Monthly reports of water use and conservation activities by urban retail water suppliers, which are generally defined as agencies serving over 3,000 service connections or deliveries 3,000 acre-feet of water annually for municipal purposes.

distribution.description:
Per-water-system data from the Clearinghouse for urban retail water suppliers, from January 2023 onwards. One row per water system per reporting period. 

Column header names have been reformatted to eliminate spaces and special characters.
distribution.title: Per-Water-System Supply and Demand, Jan2023 onwards

distribution.description:
Reported actions to respond to drought/water shortage and/or encourage conservation, as reported in the DRINC Portal monthly report. In this format, the actions are reported as a comma-separated list under the following categories: 

- demand reduction
- supply augmentation
- water restrictions
- communication
- addressing water waste
- other
distribution.title: Conservation Actions, Listed Subcategory Format

distribution.description:
Per-supplier reports of selected production and deliveries fields, comprising of a combination of data from the DRINC Portal (June 2014-December 2022) and the SAFER Clearinghouse (January 2023 onwards). This table contains values converted to gallons from the original reported units. The per-water-system data for January 2023 can be viewed in the [Per-Water-System Supply and Demand](https://data.ca.gov/dataset/urws-conservation-supply-demand/resource/264c7888-f7eb-42b4-9a19-ceb162f3ae8a) table in the original units. 

Column header names have been reformatted to eliminate spaces and special characters.
distribution.title: Per-Supplier Water Supply and Demand

distribution.description: This dataset represents a water shortage vulnerability analysis performed by DWR using modified PLSS sections pulled from the Well Completion Report PLSS Section Summaries. The attribute table includes water shortage vulnerability indicators and scores from an analysis done by CA Department of Water Resources, joined to modified PLSS sections. This leads to the most recent analysis.
